newsitem.title: USA: Nasdaq ends lower amid profit-taking in techs.
newsitem.headline: Nasdaq ends lower amid profit-taking in techs.

text.p: Nasdaq shares ended lower for the second straight session as profit-taking in many large capitalization technology stocks pressured the market.

The Nasdaq composite index fell 13.67 points, or 1.09 percent, to close unofficially at 1235.76. Nasdaq shares have ended lower in six of the past 10 sessions. The Dow industrials slipped almost 24 points to 6540.

"The techs erased some of the gains they've been making the last couple of days. The sector is just really nervous and really jumpy, so it's tough to maintain any sort of momentum for more than a few days," one trader said.

Intel Corp lead the decline in Nasdaq shares, falling five to 137-1/4. Semiconductor stocks were weak overall, with Altera Corp falling 2-1/8 to 47-1/8 after its first quarter earnings fell short of some investors' high hopes. Atmel Corp slipped 1-7/8 to 25-5/8.
PairGain Technologies Inc plunged 4-1/8 to 25-3/4 on fears it may have trouble maintaining earnings growth momentum.
Overall, losses beat gains 2274 to 1857 on total volume of 531 million shares.
